meta.method_citation: Box-Jenkins moving-average transform of descriptors under an experimental condition, after P. Ambure, A. K. Halder, H. Gonzalez-Diaz, M. N. D. S. The condition here is the mode of administration: dev_D_i(c) = D_i - mean(D over all compounds sharing route c).

rules: No experimental number is invented, estimated or recalled from memory: every value carries the URL it was read from, the sentence it was read from and that URL's retrieval time.
A value no fetched source states is null and is listed in gaps[] with the reason.
A range in the source becomes the midpoint with relation '~' and the range is kept; 'exceeds 70%' becomes relation '>' and the derived columns propagate the bound.
In vitro values are never mixed with in vivo values, and an in vivo toxicity or activity is only attached to a row whose own route the experiment used.
Orthogonal confirmation follows the sibling repo's merge.py: a second record from a different ChEMBL assay AND a different document; rows where ChEMBL has only one are flagged orthogonal=false.
The WHO DDD is published as a unit of measurement and is never used as dose_mg.

rows.ti_basis: Computed as the brief defines it: therapeutic_index = log10(toxicity_invivo) - log10(1 / activity_invivo) = log10(563.0 mg/kg) - log10(1 / 3.5 mg/kg) = 3.2946. The activity term is an in vivo ED50 in mg/kg, i.e. a DOSE: larger means less potent. Subtracting log10(1/ED50) therefore ADDS log10(ED50), so this number is log10(TD50 x ED50) and NOT the standard log10(TD50/ED50); the two agree only when the activity term is itself a reciprocal-potency quantity (1/ED50, or an affinity such as 1/Kd in L/mol), which mg/kg is not. therapeutic_index_standard holds log10(TD50/ED50) for the same pair. Both terms are mg/kg, in vivo, species rat and matched to this row's route.
